title: Pokémon Pinball
subtitle: Jupiter / HAL Laboratory · Game Boy Color
summary: Pokémon Pinball is Jupiter and HAL Laboratory's Game Boy Color pinball game, turning the series' collecting journey into play across two themed tables. The ball is a Poké Ball, while familiar creatures supply bumpers and other features around the board. Points remain the immediate reward for keeping it moving, but encounters also build a Pokédex containing the original 151 Pokémon. The collection is preserved between games, making a successful session useful even when the ball eventually escapes the flippers and the current score can no longer grow.
body: Pokémon Pinball is Jupiter and HAL Laboratory's Game Boy Color pinball game, turning the series' collecting journey into play across two themed tables. The ball is a Poké Ball, while familiar creatures supply bumpers and other features around the board. Points remain the immediate reward for keeping it moving, but encounters also build a Pokédex containing the original 151 Pokémon. The collection is preserved between games, making a successful session useful even when the ball eventually escapes the flippers and the current score can no longer grow.

Red and Blue tables have different layouts and ways to reach their special modes. In Catch Mode, repeated bumper hits reveal a Pokémon's image before the creature appears on the table as the next target. Further hits complete the capture. Changing location alters which Pokémon can be encountered, connecting the route through table features with progress in the larger collection. The player is learning the angles of a pinball game while also looking for another useful meeting within the familiar Pokémon world.

A built-in rumble feature gives the cartridge an unusual enlarged shape and provides physical feedback while the ball rebounds around the table. The Game Boy Color's screen supplies a bright setting for the two boards, while the game's saved Pokédex gives them a shared long-term purpose. Released in 1999, Pokémon Pinball made an especially direct connection between the licence and a different genre: the object used to catch a Pokémon becomes the object controlled throughout the game, joining a small sporting action to the continuing pleasure of collecting.
